messages.author: 59ce4b83b96c74fd
messages.subject: Debugging guide
parts:
Hi I have always struggled with debugging a TMB program. My greatest issue is that the compile function returns ridiculous amounts of text and very little of it is meaningful. It would be extremely helpful if there was a guide for how to best set up the compile function such that only relevant text be returned (e.g., can you specify that just the first n errors be returned).

Currently, I have just been using the flag "-w" so warnings are not returned. However, the amount of text returned is still too much.

Any tips would be appreciated.

messages.author: 02e03030784aa6a7
messages.subject: Re: Debugging guide
parts:
If you use Rstudio, that will take you directly to the line with the first compilation error.
See details (search for Rstudio):

https://github.com/kaskr/adcomp/wiki/Code--snippets

messages.author: 00f2debfd588b763
messages.subject: Re: Debugging guide
parts:
I have started using TMB:::setupRStudio() and it is great to have something that takes you right to the line in the code where the error is. However, the compiler often hangs on some cpp files. for example simply adding any of the following cout statements causes issues. 

#include <iostream>
using std::cout;
using std::endl;
std::cout<<X[year+1]<<std::endl;
cout<<X[year+1]<<endl;

I have had several other model code that appears to cause the compiler to hang. Once it compiled with an error, then fixing the error made it hang.
 
Does anyone have any idea of what the issue is and how to fix it.
